.title: The complete gold setup in *4 steps*
.yt_title: The Complete Gold Setup in 4 Steps – Sweep, CHoCH, FVG & Entry Explained
.chapters[0].title: The complete gold setup
.chapters[0].segs[0].say: Most traders don't lose money in gold because gold is unpredictable – they lose because they enter at the wrong time.
.chapters[0].segs[1].say: In this video I'll show you a setup in four steps: market structure, liquidity, order blocks and fair value gaps. And at the end we'll put everything together in one example.
.chapters[0].segs[2].say: Important up front: this is educational content, not investment advice. Trading involves risk of loss – practise new strategies on a demo account first.
.chapters[1].title: Market *structure*
.chapters[1].hook: When is a trend really a trend?
.chapters[1].segs[0].say: Everything starts with market structure. Before you think about an entry, you need to know which way the market is moving.
.chapters[1].segs[1].say: The market rises and forms a higher high – marked on the chart as H H.
.chapters[1].segs[2].say: Then comes a pullback. The new low stays above the previous one. That's a higher low, H L.
.chapters[1].segs[3].say: Now you mark the last high. This is exactly the line that has to break for the trend to be confirmed.
.chapters[1].segs[4].say: A candle closes above the high: that's a break of structure, or BOS. Pay attention: a wick alone is not enough – the candle close is what counts.
.chapters[1].segs[5].say: The pattern repeats: a new higher low, a new break of structure. As long as that continues, you only look for buys.
.chapters[2].title: Change of *Character*
.chapters[2].hook: How to spot a trend reversal early
.chapters[2].segs[0].say: But no trend lasts forever. The change of character shows you when the direction is turning.
.chapters[2].segs[1].say: Here we see a downtrend: lower highs and lower lows.
.chapters[2].segs[2].say: The last lower high is the key line.
.chapters[2].segs[3].say: The market makes one more lower low – but the sell-off is getting weaker.
.chapters[2].segs[4].say: Then a candle closes above the last lower high. That's the change of character – the first hint of a reversal.
.chapters[2].segs[5].say: The reversal is confirmed by a higher low and a break of structure to the upside. Now the new trend is here.
.chapters[3].title: Remember *this*
.chapters[3].segs[1].say: The break of structure confirms the trend.
.chapters[3].segs[2].say: The change of character warns of a change.
.chapters[4].title: Liquidity & *sweep*
.chapters[4].hook: Why your stop loss always gets hit
.chapters[4].segs[0].say: Step two: liquidity. Big market players need counterparties for their orders – and they find them where lots of stop losses sit.
.chapters[4].segs[1].say: Here's a clear low. Right below it sit the buyers' stop losses.
.chapters[4].segs[2].say: Then a second, almost equal low. Equal lows attract liquidity like a magnet.
.chapters[4].segs[3].say: The wick pokes below. The stops are triggered – and big players buy exactly those sells.
.chapters[4].segs[4].say: The candle quickly closes back above the low. That was a sweep, not a real breakout.
.chapters[4].segs[5].say: Then the impulse to the upside follows. Anyone who sold the supposed breakout now becomes fuel for the move.
.chapters[5].title: The *order block*
.chapters[5].hook: This is where big players bought
.chapters[5].segs[0].say: Step three: the order block. It shows you where large orders were placed – and where price often reacts again.
.chapters[5].segs[1].say: First a move down. Nothing special yet.
.chapters[5].segs[2].say: Suddenly a strong impulse up. Large orders were in play here.
.chapters[5].segs[3].say: The last red candle before the impulse is the order block. The zone runs from the low to the high of that candle.
.chapters[5].segs[4].say: Later, price comes back and tests the zone.
.chapters[5].segs[5].say: The reaction comes out of the order block. The entry is taken with the stop below the zone.
.chapters[6].title: The *fair value gap*
.chapters[6].hook: This gap acts like a magnet on gold
.chapters[6].segs[0].say: Step four: the fair value gap. It forms when the market moves so fast that it skips prices.
.chapters[6].segs[2].say: Then a huge candle – the market skips several prices.
.chapters[6].segs[3].say: Between the high of the first candle and the low of the third candle a gap remains. That's the fair value gap.
.chapters[6].segs[4].say: Gold often comes back to fill this gap.
.chapters[6].segs[5].say: And from the fair value gap, price then continues in the direction of the trend.
.chapters[7].title: The *complete setup*
.chapters[7].hook: All 4 steps on one gold chart
.chapters[7].segs[0].say: Now let's put it all together – in a buy setup.
.chapters[7].segs[1].say: On the hourly chart there's an uptrend. On the five-minute chart we see a correction to the downside.
.chapters[7].segs[2].say: First building block: the sweep. The wick takes the stops below the low.
.chapters[7].segs[3].say: Second building block: the change of character on the five-minute chart – a close above the last lower high.
.chapters[7].segs[4].say: The impulse leaves a fair value gap in the discount area. That's your entry zone.
.chapters[7].segs[5].say: The entry comes on the return into the fair value gap. The stop sits below the sweep wick.
.chapters[7].segs[6].say: The target is the next high. Important: you calculate the risk-reward ratio before you enter.
.chapters[8].title: Risk & *summary*
.chapters[8].segs[0].say: A setup is only as good as your risk management.
.chapters[8].segs[1].say: Risk at most one to two percent of your account per trade.
.chapters[8].segs[2].say: Set your stop loss before you enter – and don't move it against yourself.
.chapters[8].segs[2].bullet: Set the stop loss before entering
.chapters[8].segs[3].say: Only take trades with a risk-reward ratio of at least one to two.
.chapters[8].segs[4].say: And no setup works every time. Losses are part of it – what matters is that your winners are bigger than your losers.
.chapters[9].segs[0].say: If you want to practise setups like this every day on the gold chart: join our free gold group on Telegram. You'll find the link in the description. Our bootcamp with fifty-five lessons is waiting for you there too. See you in the next video!
